newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives select committee chairman.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives select committee chairman.

text.p: Backbench members of parliament of Britain's defeated Conservative party chose Sir Archie Hamilton, a former defence minister, on Wednesday as chairman of their 1922 Committee, the body which will conduct the election of a new party leader.
"I hope I meet up to the expectations of the committee," Hamilton, who is 55 and a leading right-winger, told reporters.
John Major, crushingly defeated on May 1 in his bid for another term as prime minister, has announced his intention to step down as Conservative leader.

Six candidates have thrown their hats into the ring for the election which is expected in early summer. Under party rules the 164 MPs who survived the disastrous election which sent them into opposition for the first time in 18 years will vote on the new leader.
But local activists argue that the MPs are not representative of the party throughout the country and are demanding a say in who will be their new leader.
Hamilton said he will be discussing proposals for a change in the election rules with Robin Hodgson, chairman of the National Union which represents the voluntary sector of the party.
The 1922 committee will have to decide if it is possible to change the voting rules before the election or wait until a later date.

The committee, 75 years old this year, exists to give Tory MPs a forum in which they can criticise their leaders behind closed doors without showing public disloyalty. It takes its name from the year of a backbench revolt against participation in a coalition government.
